info.title: CawCo hub
info.description: The hub's HTTP API as the dashboard uses it, and the dashboard socket's frames (components only). Generated by `bun run openapi` in packages/hub; do not edit.

ValidationErrorResponse.description: Request validation problem. Diagnostic fields are development-only.

seq.description: The effect sequence that owns this step: `ref` N in its run.

title.description:
What the call that opened the step named it: a `run`/`spawn` step's
title, an `ask`'s question, the workflow a `workflow` call started.
Null when the call named nothing.

path.description: The path on the dashboard's own origin, e.g. `/preview/<id>/`.

items.description:
Every message on every hop. `payload` is whatever the verb carries — a neutral
message, a harness option object, a control call — passed through. The hub
routes on the envelope fields and peeks only what harness.ts names.

requestId.description: The `requestId` when the payload correlates to a permission or control reply.

action.description: What the rule does when it fires. Default `'reply'` — the only kind before this existed.

interrupt.description: `immediate` only: cut into the running turn rather than queueing.

name.description: What the rule is called in the list, and in the reply the session reads.

pattern.description: The phrase to watch for, a regular expression, or a yes/no question, as `matchKind` says.

prompt.description: `action: 'llm'` only: the operator's standing instructions for the supervisor.

repeat.description:
Fire again on every later match. Off makes the rule fire once per session
and then go quiet.

reply.description: What the session is sent when the rule fires. Ignored (and not required) when `action` is `'llm'`.

trigger.description: What starts the evaluation. Default `'pattern'` — every rule before this existed.

wholeWord.description: Phrase mode only: refuse matches that sit inside a longer word.

ackedAt.description: When a turn last ended without matching the rule again, re-arming it.

fireCount.description: Fires in a row, each in a turn that matched again. Stops at {@link RULE_FIRE_CEILING}.

status.description: `pending` means fired, and no turn has since ended without matching it.

totalFires.description: Fires over the session's whole life, which re-arming does not reset.

bytes.description: Decoded size of the resolved files, for the dashboard to show.

error.description: Why the last resolve failed, when it did.

hash.description: Content hash of the resolved files; absent until a resolve succeeds.

cwd.description:
The checkout to write into. The hub fills this in as it sends a sync —
a daemon never resolves a project id, and a machine only ever receives
the project rows that live on it.

projectId.description: The hub `projects` row this is bound to. Required unless `user`.

scope.description:
Where a fleet row applies, in Claude Code's own vocabulary:

- `user` — every machine, every project. MCP goes to `~/.claude.json`'s
  top-level `mcpServers`, skills to `~/.claude/skills/`, plugins install
  `--scope user`. The default, and what most rows want.
- `local` — one project, privately: `~/.claude.json`'s
  `projects["<cwd>"].mcpServers`, the map Claude Code already keeps per
  checkout and git never sees; plugins `--scope local`. What a
  project-bound row should be unless the reader asks to share it.
- `project` — one project, shared with whoever clones it: `.mcp.json` at
  the repo root, plugins `--scope project`. It writes inside the working
  tree, so it is never the default.

Skills have no `local` in Claude Code, so a project-bound skill lands in
`<cwd>/.claude/skills/` under either scope.

enabled.description:
A disabled hook is simply not written to any machine. Claude Code itself
has no way to disable one hook while keeping it, so this is cawco's
to provide: the row stays, the registration goes.

force.description: Set on a targeted push only: overwrite a machine copy that drifted.

hash.description: sha256 hex of the material a machine compares before writing.

id.description: Client-generated, like a rule's — the editor owns creation.

name.description: What the reader calls it. Unique across the fleet.

script.description:
A command hook's script body. CawCo writes it to a file on every machine
and points the registration at that path, so the hook travels — a machine
that has never seen this hook still runs it correctly. Absent means the
handler carries its own `command` and the reader is on their own for
getting that command onto each box.

projectId.description: The hub `projects` row this is bound to. Required unless `user`.

StreamServerMessage.description: Everything the stream protocol can put on the dashboard socket.

TranscriptBlock.description: One row of a transcript, as the hub built it.

id.description:
Stable for the life of the transcript, on every screen and after every
reload: the harness's uuid for the frame it came from (one assistant frame
is several blocks, `<uuid>:<index>`), a send's uuid, `task:<id>` for a
task line — and a hash of the frame for the few that carry no uuid.

metadata.description: Everything a renderer may need beyond `content`, keyed by the kind that uses it.

parentToolUseId.description: The Task call whose subagent said this. Absent on the main transcript.

queued.description: A send not read yet ({@link TranscriptPage.queued}).

sdkUuid.description: The harness's own uuid for the frame — the handle for rewind and fork.

state.description: A send's row: where its record stands.

timestamp.description:
When the turn happened, ISO-8601. A send: when the hub accepted it.
Anything else: when the harness stored its record. Absent when the
harness gives none — an invented clock would date a row by when it was read.

TranscriptBranch.description:
A subagent's branch: the Task call it hangs under, and how far it has got.
Its blocks are the blocks whose `parentToolUseId` is {@link toolUseId}.

lastEventAt.description: When the last branch event arrived, ISO-8601, for recency sorting.

model.description: Model that answered (wire id from assistant frames), or the requested alias until the first frame arrives.

taskId.description: The task the `task_*` progress messages report under.

toolUseId.description: The Task tool.use id that spawned this subagent.

TranscriptEvent.description:
One change to a transcript, in the order the hub made it. Applied in
sequence to the page a client fetched, it gives exactly the blocks the hub
holds.

busy.description: A turn is in flight, as the frames show it.

currentTool.description: The main loop's tool in flight, cleared by its result or the turn's end.

openBlock.description: Which content block the main loop has open right now, from the partials.

streaming.description: Partial assistant text of the main loop, between partials and the final message.

streams.description: Partial assistant text, per subagent branch, by its Task call id.

thinkingClosing.description: The SDK signed the thinking block: it is wrapping up, not still going.

thinkingSince.description: When the open thinking block started, epoch ms, by the hub's clock.

thinkingStream.description: What the open thinking block has reasoned so far.

commands.description: The `/` menu: names as the session lists them, which are skills, and their details once pushed.

harness.description: The harness the frames came from.

initialized.description: The transcript has turns in it: the session has already started.

inits.description: How many `init`s this transcript has seen since the hub built it.

lastCompaction.description: What the last compaction did, from the frames that reported it.

lastTurnFailed.description: The last turn came back an error — the SDK's `is_error`.

model.description: Which model answers the next turn, by the newest `init` or fallback.

permissionMode.description: How the session answers tool permissions, by the newest `init`.

sdkStatus.description: The session's own word on what it is doing: `compacting`, `requesting`, or nothing.

sessionId.description: The harness session key the newest `init` named.

tooling.description: The servers and tools the newest `init` announced.

totalCost.description: The cumulative cost the latest `result` reported, in dollars.

turnsEnded.description: How many turns have ended since the hub built this transcript.

TranscriptPage.description:
One page of a session's transcript, newest first. The newest page carries
the live state too, and the stream position it is consistent with: a client
subscribes with `afterSeq: seq` and applies the events after it.

blocks.description: The main transcript's blocks on this page, oldest first.

branches.description: The branches whose Task call is on this page, each with its blocks.

cursor.description: Pass as `before` for the page older than this; null at the conversation's start.

facts.description: Newest page only: what the session has said about itself.

queued.description: Newest page only: the sends waiting to be read.

seq.description: Newest page only: the stream position this page is consistent with.

tail.description: Newest page only: the live tail.

TranscriptStreamFrame.description: A transcript event batch, as it rides a session's Ledger stream.

Envelope.description:
Every message on every hop. `payload` is whatever the verb carries — a neutral
message, a harness option object, a control call — passed through. The hub
routes on the envelope fields and peeks only what harness.ts names.

requestId.description: The `requestId` when the payload correlates to a permission or control reply.

FramePayload.description:
`frames`: everything a session produces, flowing agent→hub→dashboard. The
`frame` kind is a neutral message; `raw` on it carries the harness's own
event verbatim.

path.description: The path on the dashboard's own origin, e.g. `/preview/<id>/`.

kind.description:
Hub-originated: a send's record, as it stands after its latest change
— accepted, read, failed or replaced. Sequenced into the session's
stream at the moment of the change, which is where a read send's row
sits.

Daemon-originated: one send did not go — the harness refused it, or
there was nothing to hand it to — with the words that say why. The
hub fails that send's record; the session, if any, goes on.

Hub-originated: every session it still lists, pushed whenever one of the
rows moves.

path.description: The path on the dashboard's own origin, e.g. `/preview/<id>/`.

kind.description:
Hub-originated: what moved since the last publish. A dashboard gets
the whole board once, as `instances`, when it connects; after that
only the rows that changed ride along — the board is hundreds of rows
and a publish usually moves one. Everything else in the frame is the
same small snapshot the `instances` frame carries.

path.description: The path on the dashboard's own origin, e.g. `/preview/<id>/`.

requestKind.description: `tool` for a permission, `question` for an AskUserQuestion-shaped prompt.

raisedAt.description:
When the hub first parked this ask, ms epoch. Stamped by the hub
(`Pending.remember`) and kept across the daemon's replays, so every
dashboard orders and ages an ask by the same moment. Absent only on
the daemon → hub leg, before the hub has seen it.

toolUseId.description:
The tool call the ask gates, as its transcript message names it
(`toolCallId`): while the ask is parked, that call's row is the card.

kind.description:
An ask is over, whoever settled it. Daemon → hub when the harness
settled it itself (answered in its own UI, or cancelled by an
interrupt); hub → every dashboard each time a parked ask leaves the
hub's pending list — answered from any device, Telegram, a parent
session or a workflow, timed out, or dropped with its process — so no
client keeps a card nobody can answer.

Hub-originated: every machine's latest limit reading and the fleet's
spend, pushed on each agent usage report (USAGE-SPEC.md §6.4), which
is when spend lands. Small by design — the heavy aggregates are
pulled over REST.
Authoritative daemon confirmation, never merely delivery of a stop request.
Recovery found no live handle; stored conversations remain resumable.
No `instanceId` when the call it answers was machine-scoped.
Hub-originated routing failures (e.g. target machine offline).

verb.description: The whole agent↔hub↔dashboard protocol. Adding a verb is a design decision.

kind.description:
Daemon-originated: a session pushing text straight to the owner's
Telegram, with no ask to settle and nothing to answer. The hub hands it
to the bridge; the owner replying to it reaches the session, as with
any bridged message.

attachments.description: Absolute paths of images on the session's machine to send alongside.

kind.description:
Daemon-originated: one instance's coarse now-state, throttled to ~1/sec.
Broadcast — every dashboard wants the rail's word on every session, not
only the ones it has open.

Hub-originated: a work item as it stands after its latest change —
started, running, finished, dismissed. `instanceId` is its parent's.

Hub-originated: a line of delegate traffic the moment it is recorded.
`instanceId` is the delegate's.
Hub-originated: a supervisor verdict the moment it is logged.
Hub-originated, never stored: the supervisor began evaluating.

SpawnPayload.description:
`spawn`: start a session on a harness. `harness` chooses the adapter (absent
means `claude`, for every caller written before harnesses existed); `options`
rides through to that adapter verbatim — only the callbacks the agent must own
itself (`canUseTool`/permission hooks, abort) are filled in on arrival, since
functions do not survive the wire. `resume` is the harness-neutral way to
re-open or fork a stored session; `persistSession: false` asks for a session
that is never stored (a side quest's transcript).

bootstrap.description:
Start from a repository instead of a directory that is already there: the
agent clones `repo` — `owner/name`, or any URL git understands — into a
subdirectory of `baseDir` and runs the session in the clone.

canDelegate.description:
Whether this session may spawn sessions of its own (`delegate` and
`start_session`). Set by the `delegate` tool's `can_delegate` param; a
delegate that is not granted it is a leaf: claude and pi never give it the
spawning tools, and the hub refuses any spawn naming it as parent. Absent
on a session nobody delegated (a mainline session may always delegate).

denyTools.description:
Tools this session may never call, beyond whatever the harness already
denies. Set by a resolved {@link DelegateType}'s own `denyTools`; the
claude adapter merges it into the `disallowedTools` it already assembles.

effort.description:
How hard that model thinks, and how much it spends doing it. Hoisted for
the same reason again — and it is the third setting a `setEffort`
{@link ControlPayload} can still move mid-session. Absent leaves the level
to the harness, which is not the same as asking for its default: only the
model knows which stops it has.

harness.description: Which harness runs the session. Absent = `claude`.

model.description:
Which model answers, from the session's first turn. Hoisted for the same
reason as `permissionMode`. Absent leaves the choice to the harness.

options.description: Harness-specific spawn options, passed through verbatim.

parent.description:
The session this spawn is a delegate of: the child nests under it in every
rail, and `toolUseId` names the delegating tool call so the parent
transcript can render the round trip.

permissionMode.description:
How the session answers tool permissions. Hoisted out of `options` because
it is the one option the user keeps choosing — and the only one they can
still change afterwards, with a `setPermissionMode` {@link ControlPayload}.

persistSession.description: `false` asks the harness never to store this session's transcript.

projectId.description: The project this session was started from, when it was started from one.

reattachOnly.description: Existing custody only: `busy` recovers active turns; `inspect` only reports them.

requestId.description:
Correlates the `control_result` frame the agent answers the spawn with, once
the session is in place.

resume.description:
Re-open (or fork) a stored session. `sessionKey` is the harness's own
session id; `fork` reads the origin conversation into a new one; `atMessage`
resumes up to and including that assistant turn (a rewind anchor).

scratch.description:
A side quest (NEW.md §1): throwaway work. `worktree` runs the session in a
detached git worktree of `baseCwd` (the spawn's `cwd` when absent) so the
experiment cannot touch the checkout the mainline session is using.

sessionCredential.description: Hub-minted session credential: delivery only, never transcript or instance metadata.

skills.description:
Skill names to load natively before the first prompt. Each harness loads
them via its own mechanism — opencode sends `/skill` commands, claude pushes
them into the input stream — so the delegate session sees the skill the same
way it would if the user had typed the slash command.

spawnedBy.description:
The session that asked for this spawn — provenance, not nesting. Unlike
{@link parent}, it neither nests the child nor routes reports; it is what
the hub checks {@link canDelegate} against, so a leaf cannot `start_session`
its way around the rule.

title.description:
What the session is for, one line — a delegate's brief headline. Display
only.

workspace.description:
The workspace whose boundary every shell command of this session runs
inside. Set on each spawn of a work item's session — the first, and every
restore, revive and relaunch after it — and on no other session. A
machine that cannot hold the boundary refuses the spawn and says why.

StopPayload.description: `stop`: interrupt and close a live session.

discard.description: Explicitly abort unadopted custody too, then tear down side-quest resources.

from.description: The instance a fleet-originated stop claims as its caller; the hub honours the call only when the target is that instance's own delegate.

requestId.description: Correlates the `control_result` frame confirming stop/discard or its failure.

ControlPayload.description:
`control`: invoke a named method on a live session, or on the machine when
`instanceId` is absent. The method is one of the neutral names in harness.ts
({@link CONTROL_INTERRUPT}, …) plus {@link RESOLVE_PERMISSION}; the reply
comes back as a `control_result` frame carrying the same `requestId`.

Machine-scoped, `method` names either a session-catalog operation — routed to
whichever harness owns the id (`harness`, or merged across all when listing)
— or a machine feature (`listRepos`, `installTool`, the fleet controls). With
no `instanceId` and no `harness`, `listSessions` merges every harness.

from.description: The instance a fleet-originated control claims as its caller; the hub honours the call only when the target is that instance's own delegate.

harness.description: The harness the machine-scoped call is addressed at; session calls route by instance.

FsPayload.description:
`fs`: the machine's files, for the cwd picker and light markdown editing
(NEW.md §6) — not a file transfer. `list` answers with {@link FsEntry}[],
`read` with the file's text, `write` with the byte count it wrote, `image`
with an {@link FsImage} — the one binary the tunnel carries, so a picture an
agent pointed at can be looked at without the agent spending tokens on it.

content.description: `write` only: the text the file is replaced with.

FsEntry.description: One dirent of an `fs list`. `size` is 0 for a directory.

FsImage.description: What an `fs image` answers with: the file's bytes, base64, and what they are.

SendPayload.description: `send`: one turn of input for a live session's prompt stream.

attachments.description:
Text the user pasted rather than typed, kept out of `message` so the agent
can fold it into the turn as quoted material the model won't mistake for
the sentence around it.

from.description: The instance a fleet-originated send claims as its caller.

images.description: Images the turn carries: base64, with no `data:` URI prefix.

message.description: The user turn, under the uuid it keeps everywhere it is shown.

urgent.description:
Force delivery: a busy claude session reads it mid-turn via `streamInput`;
opencode/pi interrupt the turn and deliver it as the immediate next one. The
hub honours urgency only when the target is `from`'s own delegate; otherwise
it downgrades to a normal queued send.

ReposResult.description:
What the machine-scoped `listRepos` control answers with. The GitHub CLI is
the machine's own credential store — cawco never holds a token.

UpdateReport.description:
What an {@link UPDATE_CAWCO} run did. Every field is what actually
happened, not what was asked for.

changed.description:
The services whose code the update changed: the only ones it rebuilt or
restarted, and the only way a deploy leaves the agent owing a restart.
Every service when nothing was pulled (an update asked of a current
checkout restarts the stack) and for a registry install.

pulled.description: The tail of what git said — 'Already up to date.' included.

skipped.description: Why something asked for did not happen.

NeutralSessionInfo.description: A stored session as the catalog lists it. `harness` says who owns the id.

ModelInfo.description: One model a harness offers. `value` is the wire id; `resolvedModel` the alias.

contextWindow.description:
The model's context window in tokens, exactly as the harness reports it
(opencode's provider `limit.context`, pi's `Model.contextWindow`, and for
claude the `modelUsage` window the hub last observed). Absent means
unknown — never a guess.

defaultEffort.description:
The effort the CLI applies when a spawn omits effort, measured by the
harness. Null when the model takes none; absent when not measured.

released.description: ISO date the model was released, when the catalog source says.

supportsEffort.description:
Whether this model has an effort scale, and which of its stops it reaches.
The pair is the *only* thing that decides what an effort control offers —
`xhigh` and `max` are model-dependent, and a hardcoded list of which models
have them is a list that is wrong by the next release.

SupportedCommands.description:
What {@link CONTROL_SUPPORTED_COMMANDS} answers, on every harness: the
session's `/` menu. A harness with no slash commands (pi) answers an empty
list, never nothing, so the menu reads one shape whoever answered.

AuthState.description:
Whether a machine's daemon can actually start sessions for a harness.
`unreadable-credentials` is macOS's own failure: Claude Code keeps its
credentials in the login keychain, and a daemon outside the GUI session is
refused the secret (`errSecInteractionNotAllowed`). Generalized: every
harness reports its own auth word through the same three states.

NeutralTask.description:
One task of a session's plan, as every harness can express. Claude Code keeps
a ledger file per task; opencode has a native `todo` list; pi has neither.
The dashboard renders this one shape regardless of which answered.

at.description: When this was learnt, ms epoch.

detail.description:
`failed`: the tail of the installer's stderr. `unsupported`: what is
missing, named exactly — 'needs npm (Node 20+)' beats a grey chip.

method.description: The {@link ToolInstallMethod.label} that installed it or failed trying.

DelegateType.description: One named preset. `name` is the key a `delegate` call's `type` asks for.

canDelegate.description:
Whether a delegate of this type may itself delegate (or start sessions)
when the `delegate` call did not say. `false` (and absent) means a leaf —
the same default a bare `delegate` call gets; `true` makes the type a
coordinator by default. An explicit `can_delegate` on the call still wins.

description.description: What the calling model reads to decide whether this is the right type.

effort.description: How hard the model thinks: the same {@link EffortLevel} scale every other effort control uses.

name.description: Unique across the fleet; what a `delegate` call's `type` param names.

addresses.description: Tailscale first, then every non-internal IPv4 the hub's machine has.

sshPublicKey.description: The public key the hub's SSH adds sign in with, or null when it has none.

JoinAddress.description: One address a machine could reach this hub on.

label.description: Where it came from: `Tailscale`, `Tailscale DNS`, or an interface name.

url.description: `http://host:port`, the hub's REST base as seen from that address.

SshJoinJob.description: `GET /api/machines/ssh/:id`: one SSH add, as the hub holds it in memory.

lines.description: Everything the SSH session printed, stdout and stderr in arrival order.

machineId.description: From the `joined as` line, once it has been printed.

state.description: `done` means the script exited 0 and the hub has the machine online.
A template; text that parses as a JSON object or array goes as structured state.

effort.description:
How hard the model thinks, and how much it spends doing it: Claude Code's
effort scale, in its own order. Hand-written rather than tunnelled from the
SDK — nothing in this file imports a harness SDK, and `@cawco/core` has no
dependencies at all — but it is the SDK's `EffortLevel` verbatim, so the
claude adapter hands it straight on.

Effort is not only thinking depth. A lower level also buys fewer and more
consolidated tool calls, less preamble and terser confirmations; a higher one
spends tokens in all of those places. A harness with no such knob reports
`effort: false` rather than mapping onto this.

JevNodeQuestion.description:
One question on a Jev node, as the editor holds it. Choice options are rows
(name + meaning) so a half-typed option can exist while it is edited; the
compiler turns them into the API's `{ name: meaning }` criteria.

WorkflowAsk.description:
The question a `waiting` run is parked on. Self-contained on purpose: a
code-origin run has no graph to read the question off, so the hub sends the
whole thing, on the run detail and on the frame that announces the wait.

answerSchema.description:
JSON Schema for a typed answer, when the program gave `w.ask` an `answer`
schema: the answer then carries a `value` validated against it.

WorkflowFailure.description: How a typed rejection crosses the worker boundary and comes back.

WorkflowEffectKind.description: Every effect kind the bridge can carry: one `w.*` call.

AgentRow.description:
A machine from the hub's `agents` table — what `GET /api/agents` answers with,
and what rides alongside the sessions in an `instances` frame.

auth.description: `unknown` until a daemon that probes has registered at least once.

build.description: The cawco build this machine's daemon is running (NEW.md §12).

deploy.description:
Where this machine's deployment clone stands against the branch it deploys
from, as its daemon last said (PLAN.md contract C8). Absent from a daemon
that predates the deployment channel and from one whose watcher has never
ticked, which a reader must render as *nothing to report* — never as
"current". Live, not history: the hub holds it only for as long as it holds
the socket that asserted it.

harnesses.description: What each installed harness can do, as the daemon reported at register.

lastSeenAt.description: A `Date` inside the hub, the ISO string it serialises to everywhere else.

restarted.description:
True on exactly the one `instances` frame that follows this machine's
daemon coming back up because the deploy poller's idle-gated restart
fired (update.ts's `restartAgentNow`) — never for a manual restart, a
crash, or a plain boot. The hub deletes its own record of this the
instant it is read, so it never rides a later, unrelated broadcast: a
reader that was not subscribed for that one frame simply never learns
about it, the same as anyone who was not looking at the terminal when it
happened. What the dashboard's per-machine toast is keyed on.

tools.description: Last-known workflow-tool status by tool id (NEW.md §10).

BuildInfo.description: What a daemon reports about the checkout it was started from.

commit.description: Short git SHA, when the checkout is a git one.

dirty.description: Whether that checkout has uncommitted changes.

startedAt.description: When this daemon started, ms epoch.

detail.description: One sentence, exactly what `describeDeploy(state)` said about it.

failure.description: What the update flow threw, if it threw.

kind.description:
`diverged` is the one that must survive the trip intact: it means the clone
refused to update because a reset would destroy commits nobody else has,
and a refusal nobody is shown is the same as no refusal at all.

updated.description: Whether the last poll actually ran the update flow.

DeployKind.description:
Where a deployment clone stands, flattened for the wire. The kinds are
`DeployState['kind']` in packages/agent/src/deploy.ts; the rest of that
union's fields are already spoken in {@link DeployInfo.detail}, which is what
`describeDeploy` produced for this very state.

FleetSyncReport.description:
A machine's answer to `syncFleetConfig`, and what `agents.fleet` stores:
every desired entry, by the same keys the config used.

at.description: When the sync ran, ms epoch.

have.description:
What this machine now holds, by hash — the content-carrying rows only.

It is what lets the next config leave those bytes out. A machine that
cannot answer (an older daemon) simply claims nothing, and is sent
everything, which is exactly the behaviour it had before.

hooks.description:
The fleet's hooks, by the same id the hub keeps them under. Absent from a
daemon that predates them. `failed` covers three different machine-local
facts — a hand-edited script, a validation the hub already passed but this
row failed again, or a project hook with no checkout here — and `detail`
is what tells them apart.

mcpByHarness.description: Per-harness runtime truth, before the machine row's worst-state aggregation.

memoryDocs.description:
The linked documents, by the same path the set keyed them under. Absent
from a daemon that predates the set; one drifted document says so on its
own row, with the main file still `applied` beside it.

memoryHook.description:
The SessionStart hook that shows a session the document for the model it is
running. Absent from a daemon that predates the set, and from one the set
gave nothing to register.

skills.description: Absent from a daemon that predates directly-fetched skills.

toolchain.description:
The CLIs this sync leaned on, so a failure can be attributed to a binary
rather than to the machine as a whole. Absent from a daemon that predates
it, and from one that found nothing to report.

FleetItemState.description:
What one desired entry came to on one machine. `removed` is a success: the
row was disabled or deleted and the machine no longer has it — reported
once so the dashboard can say so, gone from the next report.

detail.description: `failed`: what the write or the CLI said — the tail of it.

FleetToolchain.description: The CLIs a machine's sync leaned on, by the name they are known under.

claude.description: Every `claude` this machine has; the one the sync ran is marked `used`.

CliInstall.description:
One install of a CLI a sync depends on, as the machine found it.

The reason this exists: a machine may carry several `claude` binaries at
once (a homebrew one, an npm-global one, the local installer's), PATH picks
whichever comes first, and a CLI too old for a flag the sync passes fails
with a sentence that names neither the binary nor its version. Reporting the
install makes that a fact on the dashboard rather than an expedition.

path.description: Absolute path of the executable, resolved through any symlink.

used.description: Set on the one the sync actually ran — the binary a failure came out of.

version.description: What `--version` said, when it would say.

HarnessReport.description: What a machine knows about one harness: is it installed, can it work, what can it do.

authReason.description: Why sign-in is unavailable or could not be checked, without credential data.

models.description:
The models this harness offers on this machine.

It rides the machine's report for the same reason {@link * HarnessCapabilities.permissionModes} does, and not the {@link * CONTROL_SUPPORTED_MODELS} control beside it: the catalog is a property of
the installed CLI and the account behind it, identical for every session on
the machine and knowable with none running. Asking a session for it made a
fleet-wide fact inherit one session's lifecycle — a machine with nothing
running had no catalog at all, so its model picker was empty and no session
could be named or shown an effort scale.

Absent (not empty) from a machine whose agent predates the field, and from
a harness that could not be probed; empty means it was asked and offered
nothing.

version.description: The CLI/SDK version, when it can be read.

HarnessCapabilities.description: What a harness can do, so the dashboard gates features instead of guessing.

effort.description: The reasoning-effort scale, at spawn and mid-session.

fleet.description: The harness applies the hub's fleet config (MCP/skills/memory/agents) to its own files.

fork.description: Fork a stored session into a new one.

tagSession.description: The scratch-tag the catalog filter reads.

PermissionMode.description: How a session answers tool permissions. The union is Claude Code's; others map onto it.

HarnessKind.description: The harnesses cawco can spawn sessions on. Adding one is a new adapter.

EffortLevel.description:
How hard the model thinks, and how much it spends doing it: Claude Code's
effort scale, in its own order. Hand-written rather than tunnelled from the
SDK — nothing in this file imports a harness SDK, and `@cawco/core` has no
dependencies at all — but it is the SDK's `EffortLevel` verbatim, so the
claude adapter hands it straight on.

Effort is not only thinking depth. A lower level also buys fewer and more
consolidated tool calls, less preamble and terser confirmations; a higher one
spends tokens in all of those places. A harness with no such knob reports
`effort: false` rather than mapping onto this.

ContinuationJob.description:
A "continue in new session" the hub is carrying, as every dashboard follows
it: summarise the source, then start the target seeded with the summary.
The hub owns it from the POST that starts it to its end; only a Cancel
(`DELETE /api/continuations/:id`) stops it.

summariserInstanceId.description: Absent when the source is short enough that nothing is summarised.

SessionTooling.description: What a session's `init` says about its MCP servers and tools.

ConfigInspection.description:
What a session started in `cwd` would actually see, and what a machine has
outside any project when `cwd` is absent. The answer to two questions the
dashboard asks: "what is on this machine that cawco does not manage?" and
"what will this folder give me?" — asked the moment a folder is chosen.

memory.description:
The machine's own user CLAUDE.md, or null when it has none. `managed` says
cawco wrote what is there — an unmanaged one is worth adopting. `docs`
is whatever the machine has under `~/.claude/memories/`, read the same way
and absent from a daemon that predates the set.

DiscoveredMcp.description:
One MCP server a machine really has, wherever it came from. What
{@link INSPECT_CONFIG} reports — the fleet's own rows included, so a reader
sees one list rather than two halves of one.

managed.description: Whether cawco wrote it — an unmanaged row is one worth adopting.

shadowedBy.description:
Set when a nearer scope defines the same name and wins. Claude Code's own
precedence is local > project > user, and a fleet server quietly shadowed
by a checkout is the kind of thing a reader should be told, not debug.

FleetMcpConfig.description:
A serializable MCP server definition — the SDK's own config shapes minus the
in-process `sdk` kind, which cannot cross a wire. Stored verbatim in the
hub and written verbatim into `~/.claude.json`; `${VAR}` expansion inside
is the CLI's own affair.

McpStdioServerConfig.description: MCP server config shapes, re-declared so `fleet.ts` stops importing the SDK.

FleetScope.description:

  `--scope user`. The default, and what most rows want.

DiscoveredSkill.description: One skill a machine really has. `plugin` skills come from an installed plugin.

description.description: The SKILL.md front matter's `description`, when it has one.

path.description: Absolute path of the skill's directory, for the reader and for adoption.

BlockMetadata.description: Everything a renderer may need beyond `content`, keyed by the kind that uses it.

askRequestId.description: A `user.delegate_ask`'s hub permission requestId — what it waits on to be answered.

attachments.description: Files the reader attached to the turn, parsed back out of its `<pasted-text>` blocks.

delegateInstanceId.description: The delegate a `tool.handoff` started, read once off its result.

delegateTitle.description: The delegate's brief headline, carried beside {@link delegateInstanceId}.

images.description: A stored transcript can name an image it no longer carries, hence the optional src.

noteKind.description: Harness-injected user-role content (task notifications, reminders, compaction).

noteTaskToolId.description: A task notification's Task `tool_use_id` — folds the note into its branch.

peerName.description: Its display name, as the sender's host asserted it.

peerSession.description: The sender's host-openable session, so the card can link back to it.

permissionMode.description: `init` only, and re-reported every turn: what the session answers tools with.

reportKind.description: Set when a `user.peer` is a delegate's auto-report rather than a hand-off.

resultImages.description: Images returned by the tool, as the hub's media references.

ruleName.description: A `user.rule`'s rule name, read off its `[Rule: <name>]` marker line.

sendFailed.description: Why a send did not go: its record's reason.

skills.description: `init` only: which of the commands are skills rather than commands.

slashCommands.description: `init` only: what this session answers behind `/`, without the leading slash.

subagentModel.description: The `model` override the spawn input asked for, when present.

thinkingDurationMs.description:
How long the thinking block ran, measured by the hub's clock between the
block opening and its settled message. Preferred over transcript
adjacency, which reads 0 when thinking and a tool call land in one frame.

tooling.description: `init` only: the MCP servers and tools behind the `/` palette.

toolUseResult.description: The reader's answers to an `AskUserQuestion`, normalised by the harness adapter.

urgent.description: A send made urgently (`SendRecord.mode`): into the running turn, or ahead of it.

workflowEvent.description: Set when a `user.peer` is a workflow's notice: what happened, e.g. `step Build failed`.

BlockTooling.description: The MCP servers and tools an `init` announced.

UserQuestionAnswered.description:
A question the reader answered: the questions asked and the choices made,
keyed by question text.

`answers` values are `string | string[]` by wire truth: the Claude SDK types
them `string` ("multi-select answers are comma-separated") but a real
transcript carries an array for a multi-select answer, and freeform "Other"
text lands inside `answers` too — so a value is not guaranteed to match any
option `label`. The union is the truth; nothing coerces it.

annotations.description: Per-question notes (preview selections), keyed by question text.

response.description: Freeform text the reader typed instead of selecting a structured option.

UserAnswers.description: The reader's choices, back the way the tool reads them.

UserQuestion.description: One question of an `AskUserQuestion`-shaped prompt, as every harness can express.

UserQuestionDismissed.description:
A question the reader walked away from. Every harness expresses this as a
denial of the question's permission, and it carries no answers at all — so
it is a separate member rather than an answered result with an empty map,
which would let a consumer draw a card with blank choices and call it an
answer.

BlockType.description: What a block is: the row kind a renderer draws it as.

TranscriptPageBranch.description: A subagent branch with its own blocks, as a page carries it.

TranscriptFacts.description: What the session has said about itself, kept beside its blocks.

commands.description: The `/` menu: names as the session lists them, which are skills, and their details once pushed.

harness.description: The harness the frames came from.

initialized.description: The transcript has turns in it: the session has already started.

inits.description: How many `init`s this transcript has seen since the hub built it.

lastCompaction.description: What the last compaction did, from the frames that reported it.

lastTurnFailed.description: The last turn came back an error — the SDK's `is_error`.

model.description: Which model answers the next turn, by the newest `init` or fallback.

permissionMode.description: How the session answers tool permissions, by the newest `init`.

sdkStatus.description: The session's own word on what it is doing: `compacting`, `requesting`, or nothing.

sessionId.description: The harness session key the newest `init` named.

tooling.description: The servers and tools the newest `init` announced.

totalCost.description: The cumulative cost the latest `result` reported, in dollars.

turnsEnded.description: How many turns have ended since the hub built this transcript.

kind.description: What the harness says this is, when it knows. Absent → derived from the name and the session's skill list.

NeutralStatus.description: A session's own word on what it is doing right now.

The live tail: what the turn is doing between frames. The one part of a
transcript that moves token by token.

busy.description: A turn is in flight, as the frames show it.

currentTool.description: The main loop's tool in flight, cleared by its result or the turn's end.

openBlock.description: Which content block the main loop has open right now, from the partials.

streaming.description: Partial assistant text of the main loop, between partials and the final message.

streams.description: Partial assistant text, per subagent branch, by its Task call id.

thinkingClosing.description: The SDK signed the thinking block: it is wrapping up, not still going.

thinkingSince.description: When the open thinking block started, epoch ms, by the hub's clock.

thinkingStream.description: What the open thinking block has reasoned so far.

ToolGlance.description: The tool a session is running right now — the fleet view's glance line.

TranscriptWhere.description: Where a transcript was found: the machine, folder, key and harness.

Verb.description: The whole agent↔hub↔dashboard protocol. Adding a verb is a design decision.

DelegateEvent.description:

the system of record: the transcript markers say the same things, but only

payload.description: The tool input as the harness asked it — `{filepath, diff}`, `{questions}`, …

createdAt.description: When the hub recorded it, as JSON carries a date.

id.description: The hub's row id — what a fold deduplicates on and orders by.

requestId.description: The permission request an ask and its answer share. Null on a report.

firstLines.description: The first line of each: what it was asked, what it reported, why it failed.

bin.description: The executable whose presence means installed.

dependencyOnly.description:

the policy list until something needs them, and the dashboard shows them
only where they explain another tool's state.

install.description: Ordered by preference. Empty for a platform = unsupported there.

requires.description:

automatically (depth 1 — requirements do not have requirements); one that

versionCommand.description: Probe for the version; the first `x.y.z` in its output is the answer.

wellKnownPaths.description:
Where installers put the binary when it lands off the daemon's PATH —
probed with `~` expanded, after `which` misses. An installer that edits
shell rc files fixes the *user's* PATH, never a daemon that is already
running.

ToolInstallMethod.description:

command.description:

label.description: Names the method in status and errors: 'curl script', 'npm', 'winget'.

native.description:

needs.description:

FleetAgent.description:
The whole file. Unlike a skill's, it rides the catalog read: a definition is
a page of markdown, and an editor that has to fetch it again is a round trip
for nothing.

Phase B: daemon `syncFleetConfig` owns convergence; until then the hub pushes
over the `fs` verb, which is why this is nowhere in {@link FleetConfig}.

at.description: When the hub last stored it, ms epoch.

hash.description: sha256 hex of `content` — what tells a machine's copy apart from the fleet's.

MemoryDocRow.description:
One document the main memory links, as the dashboard reads it. Like a
subagent's file and unlike a skill's, the content rides the listing: a
document is a page of markdown, and an editor that has to fetch each one
again is a round trip for nothing.

RuleStats.description: What the list needs to show about a rule without loading every session's state.

pending.description: Sessions that fired this rule and have not yet finished a turn without it.

RuleAction.description:
What a firing rule does.

- `reply` — send {@link Rule.reply}, verbatim, the way every rule has
  always fired.
- `llm` — hand the turn to the supervisor and send back whatever it
  decides. Only fires at the `turn` timing (the supervisor judges a
  finished turn, not a half-typed message) and never repeats a fixed
  reply (it decides fresh every time).

RuleMatchKind.description:
How {@link Rule.pattern} is read.

- `phrase` / `regex` — text to find in what the session said.
- `meaning` — a yes/no question the hub puts to TypeSafe's Jev (through
  OpenRouter) about what the session said; the rule fires when the answer
  is yes. Decided by the hub asynchronously, so nothing here matches it.

RuleScope.description:
What narrows a rule from "every session on the fleet" to some of them. Every
field is optional and they are ANDed; an empty scope is the default and means
everywhere. `model` is a substring test, so `opus` covers every dated build
of it.

harness.description: The harnesses cawco can spawn sessions on. Adding one is a new adapter.

RuleTiming.description:
When the reply is delivered.

- `turn` — the session has stopped and is idle, so the reply wakes it into a
  new turn. This is the one that makes a session keep working.
- `message` — queued the moment the assistant message that matched is
  complete; the session reads it at the next turn boundary without being
  interrupted.
- `immediate` — sent the moment the phrase appears mid-stream, optionally
  interrupting the turn in flight ({@link Rule.interrupt}).

RuleTrigger.description:
What starts a rule's evaluation.

- `pattern` — the phrase/regex match this file has always done: a rule
  fires when {@link Rule.pattern} shows up.
- `every-turn` — there is nothing to match; every turn end is itself the
  trigger. Only the supervisor can act on that (see {@link RuleAction}),
  since nothing about the turn has been read yet to answer with a fixed
  reply.

RuleWatch.description: Which part of the session's output a rule reads.

RuleDraft.description: A rule as it arrives from the dashboard, before the hub gives it an id.

name.description: What the rule is called in the list, and in the reply the session reads.

repeat.description:
Fire again on every later match. Off makes the rule fire once per session
and then go quiet.

action.description: What the rule does when it fires. Default `'reply'` — the only kind before this existed.

prompt.description: `action: 'llm'` only: the operator's standing instructions for the supervisor.

pattern.description: The phrase to watch for, a regular expression, or a yes/no question, as `matchKind` says.

wholeWord.description: Phrase mode only: refuse matches that sit inside a longer word.

reply.description: What the session is sent when the rule fires. Ignored (and not required) when `action` is `'llm'`.

SupervisorEvent.description:
One line of the supervisor's intervention log — `supervisor_events`
(packages/hub `db/schema.ts`), read over `GET /api/supervisor/events` and
pushed as a `supervisor_event` frame. Silent verdicts are recorded too: the
log is the only place any of this is visible, so "it looked and did
nothing" has to show up the same as "it spoke".

id.description: The hub's row id — what a fold deduplicates on and orders by.

message.description: Sent into the session (`reply`) or shown to the operator (`escalate`/`ask`); null for the rest.

model.description: Which model answered, when one did.

note.description: The supervisor's own one-line rationale — logged, never sent to the session.

ruleId.description: The rule that fired, for `source: 'rule'`; null for autopilot.

MachineMemorySet.description:
A machine's own memory set: the user CLAUDE.md and whatever is under
`~/.claude/memories/`. What {@link READ_MEMORY_FILE} answers with, and what a
peek and an adoption read. A daemon that predates the set answers without
`docs`, which reads as a machine that keeps none.

MachineMemoryDoc.description: One linked document as a machine really has it, whoever wrote it.

MemoryVersion.description: One superseded version of the fleet's memory, as a listing reads it.

path.description: Which document of the set it was a version of; absent is the main one.

FleetHook.description:
One hook the fleet should have. Extends {@link FleetPlacement} so a hook can
be bound to a project the way an MCP server can — the scaffolding was
already there, this is the first row that reads it.

enabled.description:
A disabled hook is simply not written to any machine. Claude Code itself
has no way to disable one hook while keeping it, so this is cawco's
to provide: the row stays, the registration goes.

force.description: Set on a targeted push only: overwrite a machine copy that drifted.

hash.description: sha256 hex of the material a machine compares before writing.

id.description: Client-generated, like a rule's — the editor owns creation.

name.description: What the reader calls it. Unique across the fleet.

script.description:
A command hook's script body. CawCo writes it to a file on every machine
and points the registration at that path, so the hook travels — a machine
that has never seen this hook still runs it correctly. Absent means the
handler carries its own `command` and the reader is on their own for
getting that command onto each box.

cwd.description:
The checkout to write into. The hub fills this in as it sends a sync —
a daemon never resolves a project id, and a machine only ever receives
the project rows that live on it.

projectId.description: The hub `projects` row this is bound to. Required unless `user`.

scope.description:
Where a fleet row applies, in Claude Code's own vocabulary:

- `user` — every machine, every project. MCP goes to `~/.claude.json`'s
  top-level `mcpServers`, skills to `~/.claude/skills/`, plugins install
  `--scope user`. The default, and what most rows want.
- `local` — one project, privately: `~/.claude.json`'s
  `projects["<cwd>"].mcpServers`, the map Claude Code already keeps per
  checkout and git never sees; plugins `--scope local`. What a
  project-bound row should be unless the reader asks to share it.
- `project` — one project, shared with whoever clones it: `.mcp.json` at
  the repo root, plugins `--scope project`. It writes inside the working
  tree, so it is never the default.

Skills have no `local` in Claude Code, so a project-bound skill lands in
`<cwd>/.claude/skills/` under either scope.

A fleet hook's script as one machine really has it, whoever last wrote it.
What {@link READ_HOOK_SCRIPT} answers with.

WorkspaceState.description: A workspace's life: `active` while its checkout is kept; `archived` once its boundary and clone are gone.

UsageLimitsResponse.description: What `/api/usage/limits` returns: every machine's latest readings.

spendLimit.description:
Extra usage: the pay-as-you-go real money spent past the plan this month,
and its monthly cap, in dollars (the API's `spend.used` / `spend.limit`
money objects). Null when not reported; the cap is null with extra usage
off. `spendResetsAt` is when the cap resets (ISO), only when the API
says; null otherwise, never guessed.

stale.description: Set when a fetch failed and the caller is served the last good reading.

LimitWindow.description:
One plan window, whoever meters it. `group` names how long the window runs:
`session` is a 5-hour window (Claude's `five_hour`, OpenCode Go's `rolling`),
`weekly` runs 7 days, `monthly` runs one calendar month to `resetsAt`.
`percent` is the share USED, 0–100 (it can pass 100).

OpenCodeGoLimits.description:
The OpenCode Go plan's three windows, read from
`GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage` with the machine's `opencode-go`
key. Absent (null) on a machine with no Go key. `stale` is set when a read
failed and the last good windows are served with the error attached.

UsageSpend.description:
The fleet's real spend, as the hub reckons it and serves it at
`/api/usage/spend` and on every `kind: 'usage'` frame: the one figure every
"today" in CawCo reads.

Real money is opencode's own per-message cost; Claude is a subscription
whose constraint is a percentage, so its API-price estimate is never added
in. The days are the hub's: `todayStart` is local midnight and `weekStart`
this Monday's midnight in `timeZone`, the hub's own zone (IANA name).

UsageSummary.description: What `/api/usage/summary` returns: the groups, their totals, and unpriced models.

UsageSummaryRow.description:
One aggregated group in a usage summary. `key` is the group's identity (a
session id, a machine id, an hour's epoch ms); `label` is what a reader is
shown. Session rows carry their machine and the instance that ran them (null
for a session run outside CawCo); machine rows carry the machine.

UsageRowMachine.description: The machine a summary row ran on: named, never shown by id.

UsageTotals.description: The whole-window sums a summary's groups roll up to.

StreamBacklog.description:
Hub → client when the requested gap is inside its ring: events contiguous
ascending from `afterSeq + 1`. The client applies them in order, then
follows live deltas.

SessionStreamEvent.description:
One event on a session's canonical stream. `seq` is hub-assigned, monotonic
per session, starting at 1 — and NO GAP is ever delivered: a client that
observes `seq > lastSeq + 1` re-subscribes with `afterSeq = lastSeq` instead
of applying the delta.

sessionId.description: The instance id — what the dashboard calls a viewId.

SessionStreamFrame.description:
What a session's stream carries: the changes each frame made to its
transcript, as the hub built them (`transcript-types.ts`), and its preview's
state. Raw frames never reach a dashboard; the hub folds them.

path.description: The path on the dashboard's own origin, e.g. `/preview/<id>/`.

SendRecord.description:
THE ONE RECORD OF A SEND. The hub writes it when it accepts the send and is
its only writer after that: every change is stored, then sequenced into the
session's stream as a `send` frame, and a history read serves it beside the
entries. Every screen draws the send from this, live and after any reload.

acceptedAt.description: ISO-8601: when the hub took the send. The only clock its row shows.

anchor.description:
A failed send the harness never stored: the uuid of the last thing the
session said before it failed — an assistant frame, or a send it read.
Its row goes right after that. Absent when the hub knew of nothing the
session had said: its row then goes after the last row dated before
`acceptedAt`, or first when none is.

body.description:
Exactly what the sender submitted: its words, its pictures (as the hub's
media references) and pastes, and who it is from. What the agent adds on
the way to the harness (a worktree line, an urgent prefix) is not in it.

harnessId.description:
The id the harness stored the send under, where that is not its uuid:
opencode's message id, pi's entry id, and — for a send Claude joined into
another's record ({@link SessionMessage.joined}) — that record's uuid.

reason.description: Why it failed, in the harness's words or the hub's.

replaces.description: The failed send this one was sent in place of.

NeutralUserMessage.description:
A user-role message. Two things wear this shape: what the harness says in
the user's role (tool results, its own notices), and a message SENT to the
session — which always carries `origin` and `uuid` ({@link SentMessage}),
and nothing else does.

replaces.description:
A retry: the uuid of the failed send this one is sent in place of. The
hub marks that record `replaced` ({@link SendRecord.replacedBy}).

timestamp.description: When the harness stored it ({@link NeutralAssistantMessage.timestamp}).

questionResult.description: The answer payload of an `AskUserQuestion` tool result, normalised by the harness adapter.

SendMode.description:
How a send asks to be read: as a turn of its own, as a note the next turn
folds in (`shouldQuery: false`), or urgently — into the running turn, or
ahead of it.

SendState.description:
Where a send stands, as the hub alone decides it: waiting for the harness
(`pending`), taken up by it (`read`), never going to be (`failed`, with
why), or sent again as another send (`replaced`).

StreamReset.description:
Hub → client when the gap is unrecoverable (older than the ring holds):
an honest refusal, never a partial replay. The client reads the newest
transcript page again and resumes from the `seq` it carries.

StreamDelta.description: Hub → client, live fan-out of one sequenced event.

StreamSubscribe.description:
Client → hub. `afterSeq` present is a resume ("I have up to here — replay the
rest"): a client sends it with the `seq` its transcript page was read at, and
again after a reconnect. Absent is a fresh join ("start me from now").

CommandEnvelope.description:
Client → hub: an operator action as a durable, trackable object rather than
a fire-and-forget call. `commandId` is client-generated and unique per
submission; `payload` is exactly what the corresponding legacy relay
operation takes today.

CommandKind.description: The operations a command envelope can carry — 1:1 with existing relay ops.

contentOffset.description: Blocks already published for this message, preserving row ids across incremental settlement.

error.description:
The harness's word that this message is not the model answering but a
failure written in its place — Claude's synthetic `authentication_failed`,
`rate_limit`, … (measured on CLI 2.1.280: "Not logged in · Please run
/login" arrives as one, before an `is_error` result).

failedSends.description:
Set by the hub on an error message ({@link error}) that answered sends
the session had just read: they failed with its words, and their rows
carry them, so it draws no row of its own.

raw.description: The harness's own event, verbatim, for renderers that need more than this.

timestamp.description:
When the harness stored this record, ISO-8601: the clock its row shows,
live as after a reload ({@link SessionMessage.timestamp}). Claude's
stream carries its record's own; opencode's is its message's
`time.created`; pi's is its entry's. Absent on a frame the harness
stores no record for.

cache.description: Prompt-cache tokens the turn read from / wrote to, when the harness reports them.

failedSends.description:
The sends this error failed, set by the hub: read, and answered by nothing
but this error. Their rows carry the error, so it draws no line of its own.

recovered.description: Read from stored history during recovery, rather than a newly completed turn.

timestamp.description: When the harness stored what it closes on ({@link NeutralAssistantMessage.timestamp}).

NeutralSystemMessage.description:
A `system` frame. One loose interface rather than a subtype union: the folding
layer switches on `subtype` and reads the fields each subtype carries, and a
harness that emits a subtype nothing here names degrades to a generic line.

permissionMode.description: How a session answers tool permissions. The union is Claude Code's; others map onto it.

result.description:
task_notification: the report a finished task handed back. Claude's live
frame carries none; its stored notification (`<result>`) does.

retry.description:
provider_retry ({@link PROVIDER_RETRY}): the provider's own message, and
when the harness makes its next attempt (ms epoch) if it said.

storedAs.description:
stored ({@link MESSAGES_STORED}), or read: the id the harness stores each
send under, by the send's uuid, where the harness keys its own record
differently (opencode's message id, pi's entry id). The hub keeps it on
the send's record, so a history read finds the send again.

whole.description:
held ({@link MESSAGES_HELD}): `held` is every send the harness has been
handed. Said by an agent taking over a process that outlived the one
before it, off the process's own output: a send from before then that is
not in it never reached the process.

NeutralRawMessage.description: A frame that has no neutral meaning yet, forwarded whole for a future renderer.

autopilot.description:
The supervisor's standing autopilot for this session, set from the
composer popover. `null` means never configured; disabling keeps the
prompt rather than discarding it, so re-enabling does not mean retyping
it. Absent on a hub that predates the column.

canDelegate.description:
Whether the session may spawn delegates of its own — `false` on a leaf
delegate (spawned with `can_delegate: false`, the default). Null on a
session nobody delegated, which may.

derivedTitle.description:
The name the session's first user message gave it, derived once by the hub.
A listing already answers {@link title} with this when nothing named the
row, so a reader never watches the label change as the transcript arrives.

effort.description:
The effort the session actually sends, as its agent last read it back from
the harness ({@link import ("./harness").EFFORT_READ}): a level, `none` when
it sends no effort, null until the first reading lands. A restart hands a
level back to the new process, so it keeps working at the one it was on.

harness.description: Which harness owns {@link sessionId} — what a resume and a catalog read route on.

held.description: First-hand custody on the current agent connection, never stored liveness.

kind.description: `scratch` for a side quest; absent from a hub that predates the column.

lastError.description: What killed the session, on a row the agent reported as `error`.

parentInstanceId.description: The instance this one is a delegate of; absent for a mainline session.

parentToolUseId.description: The delegating tool call, so the parent transcript can render the round trip.

permissionMode.description:
How the session answers tool permissions and which model answers, as of its
last spawn, switch or `init`. Null on a session that has never said.

projectId.description: Set when the session was started from a project page.

runningDelegates.description: Hub-derived count of live delegated work items, including descendants and checks.

seenAt.description:
When the owner last looked at it (its tab in front, after it ended) or
archived it off Finished, on any device. Null on one never seen.

sessionId.description: The harness's own session id, once the session has named itself.

title.description:
What the session is called: the owner's rename, else the name the session
gave itself (`set_title`) or was spawned under, else {@link derivedTitle}.

titleSource.description:
Who gave the session its name: `owner` (a dashboard rename, which the
session's own `set_title` cannot replace) or `agent`. Null while nobody has.

workItemId.description:
The work item this session runs: every delegate is one, and a session
never runs more than one. Null on a session nobody delegated, and on a
delegate from before work items existed.

InstanceStatus.description:
What a session row is doing, right now, as the hub last heard it.

- `starting` — a spawn went out and hasn't been confirmed live yet.
- `running` — the owning daemon currently lists the instance.
- `sleeping` — no live process, but resumable: the harness has a session id
  to pick back up from. This is what a daemon restart or a quiet drop used
  to report as `error` with {@link RESTART_RESUMABLE} in `lastError`; that
  encoding conflated "gone but fine" with a real failure, so `sleeping` rows
  carry `lastError: null` — nothing went wrong, there's just nothing running.
- `stopped` — deliberate: the operator (or a `stop` call) ended it.
- `error` — an actual failure. `lastError` is required here, and this is
  where {@link RESTART_LOST} still lands: a restart with nothing to resume
  from is a real loss, not a nap.
- `unknown` — the machine that owns this row can't currently be reached, so
  the hub can't say which of the above is true.
- `discarded` — a side quest torn down on purpose; gone for good.

PermissionUpdate.description: A permission the SDK suggests persisting, so "always allow" has something to write.

UsageLimitsReading.description:
One machine's latest limit reading, as the hub stores it (`usage_limits`)
and broadcasts it in a `kind: 'usage'` frame. `fetchedAt` is a `Date` inside
the hub and the ISO string it serialises to on the wire.

SessionPulse.description:
A coarse, now-state the rail draws without frames: what a session is doing
right now, folded on the daemon from the frames it is already pumping. It is
the *fallback* the dashboard reads for sessions it has not subscribed to —
open sessions still render the richer frame-fed state. `activity` is the same
three words the fleet view uses; `busy`/`runningSubagents` keep the finer
signals separate so a reader can still tell "blocked" from "working".

activity.description: Coarse now-state the rail draws without frames.

at.description: ms epoch of the last frame that changed this pulse.

currentTool.description: The tool the main loop is inside, addressed as the transcript addresses it.

SupervisorStatusSignal.description:
Fired the moment an evaluation actually begins — the transient half of the
supervisor's visible life. Every evaluation is guaranteed to terminate in a
published {@link SupervisorEvent}, so a consumer can treat that event as
this signal's close; nothing here is persisted.

WorkflowFrame.description: Hub-originated run transition, separate from a harness's session frames.

ask.description: Present while the run is `waiting`: everything needed to answer it.

checkpoint.description: The marker a `w.checkpoint` call just recorded.

seenAt.description: When the owner last looked at it or archived it, on any device.

seq.description: The effect sequence that owns this step: `ref` N in its run.

title.description:
What the call that opened the step named it: a `run`/`spawn` step's
title, an `ask`'s question, the workflow a `workflow` call started.
Null when the call named nothing.

WorkspaceRef.description: A workspace as the machine that holds it is told about it.

SentMessage.description:
A message sent to a session, by the reader or by cawco. `uuid` is its one
identity from the press to a reload: the dashboard's command id for a
reader's send, minted where the hub builds its own. The hub keeps one
{@link SendRecord} under it, and every copy of the message on every screen
is drawn from that record.

RepoInfo.description: One repository a machine can {@link SpawnPayload.bootstrap} from.

ToolState.description: What a probe or an install attempt found. The unit every surface renders.
